layout_map: Dark cyan blueprint-grid background. Left two-thirds holds a large light-blue Postgres elephant logo (cells 1-2 and 5-6, center ~x230,y220, filling roughly the upper-left quadrant) with the lowercase white wordmark 'Postgres' beneath it (baseline ~y480, cells 9-10) and a mint-green rounded badge reading '18' immediately to its right (~x430,y470, cell 10). A hand-drawn coral-red script word 'huge' sits over the logo's right edge (~x420,y170, cell 6-7) with a curved red arrow pointing down-left at the elephant from ~x360,y90. A retro grinning man's photo headshot fills the right third (cells 4,8,12,16; face center ~x1080,y300) with a thin red corner-bracket frame and a faint glow.
reads_as: Postgres got a HUGE new version 18 — vintage guy is delighted
why_it_works: Hand-scrawled 'huge' + arrow injects raw emotion onto a clean product logo, and the smiling retro face signals 'good news' before any word is read
mimic_for: a major version/release of a tool lands and it's a big deal worth learning now
title: Postgres 18 just dropped. Now is the best time to learn it...

layout_map: Dark cyan grid background. Center-left mid-line carries the big lowercase headline 'specs > code' (baseline ~y360, cells 6-7), 'specs' in white, a white greater-than sign as the comparison operator, 'code' in white. A hand-drawn red script word 'really?' floats above-left at ~x300,y180 (cell 2-3) with a curved red arrow swooping down-right toward 'specs'. A black-tie skeptical/frowning man's photo headshot fills the right third (cells 4,8,12; face center ~x1080,y260) with a tiny white 'MONDAY' label tab in the top-right corner (~x1180,y40).
reads_as: Are specs really better than code? — this guy doubts it
why_it_works: The '>' operator frames a debate in one glyph and the scrawled 'really?' plus skeptical face plant doubt, baiting the click to resolve the argument
mimic_for: two approaches/tools pitted against each other where one supposedly beats the other
title: The new spec-driven workflow is a mess...

layout_map: Dark cyan grid background. Top-left a mint-outlined rounded badge reads 'MODERN' in white caps (~x320,y80, cell 2-3). Below it a huge white serif word 'Java' dominates the left-center (baseline ~y300, cells 5-6-9-10, the largest element). Beneath that a small hand-drawn mint-green script tag 'is fire' (~x340,y430, cell 10). A coral-red hand-drawn arrow points right from ~x640,y230 toward the subject. A shirtless older man in sunglasses smoking a cigarette fills the right third (cells 4,8,12; face center ~x1080,y230) with a faint 'TUTORIAL' watermark lower-right.
reads_as: Modern Java is unexpectedly cool — this cocky guy proves it
why_it_works: Giant single-word subject + the cheeky 'is fire' tag and arrow toward a confident character reframe a 'boring' language as desirable
mimic_for: an old/unfashionable technology is actually good again and worth a fresh look
title: Modern Java is pretty cool and you can't avoid it anymore...

layout_map: Dark cyan grid background. Left-center holds a giant white number '500' (baseline ~y330, cells 5-6-9, the biggest element) with white caps 'CODE LINES' stacked beneath it (baseline ~y480, cells 9-10). Above-right of the 500 a hand-drawn coral-red script price '$199' (~x480,y130, cell 6-7) with a short red arrow curving down to the number. A shocked wide-eyed doll/woman face with parted lips fills the right third (cells 4,8,12; face center ~x1050,y300) and a small 'FRIDAY' label tab sits top-right (~x1180,y40).
reads_as: 500 code lines cost $199?! — disbelief on the face
why_it_works: The giant number anchors a concrete stat, the scrawled $price adds a shock value, and the bug-eyed face supplies the emotional reaction for you
mimic_for: a surprising count or price stat lands that should feel absurd or shocking
title: The dumbest thing ever...

layout_map: Dark grid background. Two-row headline on the left: 'WEB' in big white caps (baseline ~y180, cells 1-2-5-6) and below it 'Killer' in black caps sitting on a solid yellow highlighter block (~x180,y320, cells 9-10). A wild-eyed snarling man's face (Shining-style) fills the right third (cells 4,8,12; face center ~x1020,y260, mouth bared). A small flat Go gopher mascot sits in the bottom-left corner (~x90,y620, cell 13).
reads_as: Something is a 'web killer' — and this guy is unhinged about it
why_it_works: The yellow-highlighted 'Killer' word reads as a threat and the iconic rage face supplies maximum menace; the corner mascot quietly names the subject
mimic_for: a technology threatens to kill/replace an incumbent (web, a framework, a stack)
title: WebAssembly Explained

layout_map: Near-black faint-grid background. A three-row white caps headline fills the left two-thirds: 'WHAT THEY' (baseline ~y170, cells 1-2-5), then 'DON'T' in large red caps as the accent row (baseline ~y360, cells 5-6-9, color the curiosity word), then 'TELL YOU' in white caps (baseline ~y520, cells 9-10-13). why_it_works: The classic 'what they DON'T tell you' withhold formula with the negation word burning red triggers information-gap curiosity; the animal substitutes for an emotive face

title: What's Actually Happening With JS Frameworks
